title: Readiness and liveness
summary: A readiness check asks whether a container should receive traffic. A liveness check asks whether Kubernetes should restart it.
introduction: A readiness check asks whether a container should receive traffic. A liveness check asks whether Kubernetes should restart it. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A readiness check asks whether a container should receive traffic. A liveness check asks whether Kubernetes should restart it.

blocks.code:
Readiness fails -> stop sending Service traffic to that Pod
Liveness fails repeatedly -> container may restart
blocks.title: Readiness and liveness

blocks.text: The two checks serve different purposes. A temporary dependency problem should not always trigger a restart loop.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose which check should notice that the app is still warming up.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not use a restart as the answer to every readiness problem.
For more detail later, use this [Kubernetes further reading](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/kubernetes-basics/).

seo.title: Kubernetes: Readiness and liveness
seo.description: Learn about readiness and liveness in Kubernetes. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
